e79fc332c6.q: How did tire allocation differences affect Matt Neal's competitiveness in 1990s touring cars as a privateer?
e79fc332c6.a: In the 1990s, factory teams had access to different tire suppliers while privateers did not. The first race Neal won with Max Power sponsorship in 1999 was the first time they were allowed to run with the same specification tires as the factory cars. Before that, they were handicapped by being forced to use inferior tire options, which made their victories even more remarkable to the industry observers who understood the disadvantage they were carrying.

8d6e041423.q: What was the scale of tire consumption in touring car racing during the works team era?
8d6e041423.a: A two-car works team in that era would use approximately 200 tires over a single weekend, with 100 tires per car. In modern day touring cars, a team is allowed only 16 new tires per weekend per car and eight used ones that have been carried over from previous events, representing a dramatic reduction in tire usage.

7c9ddc9cd5.q: When did AI-powered data analysis technology significantly emerge in professional motorsport?
7c9ddc9cd5.a: Basic telemetry data started to manifest in the mid-1990s, but AI and advanced data analysis have really taken off in the last 18 to 24 months. AI can now analyze video footage from television broadcast and extract detailed performance data without any insight into the car's internal workings, determining horsepower output and boost timing simply from visual analysis.

7722cf265a.q: Why did Honda end its touring car sponsorship at the end of 2020?
7722cf265a.a: EU net zero regulations and CAF emissions regulations forced Honda UK to face approximately £6,000 in fines for each Type R sold in the UK market. Since they no longer wanted to sell Type Rs due to these regulatory costs, continuing to promote the model through touring car racing no longer made commercial sense unless it was purely a brand exercise with no direct product promotion.

10dff1d2e5.q: What is the market size of classic racing in Europe?
10dff1d2e5.a: Classic racing in Europe is a billion euro industry. This sector includes modern classics aged 10 to 15 years old as well as historic vehicles like E-Types and Mark One Cortinas. The classic racing side is somewhat more insulated from net zero regulations than modern motorsport, though events like Goodwood Revival are implementing sustainable fuels and materials.
